money.title: Contact Us
money.what_it_is: The Office of the Bursar oversees the student account for all Penn State students across all campuses.
steps: Submit a request or question by clicking the button provided on the page.
money.timing: Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. ET.
money.notes: Please have your nine-digit Penn State ID number available.

money.title: Who to reach out with questions about your student account and financial aid
money.what_it_is: This page provides information on which offices to contact for questions regarding student accounts and financial aid.
money.who_to_contact: Office of the Bursar: 814-865-6528; Office of Student Aid: 814-865-6301
money.source_title: WHO TO REACH OUT WITH QUESTIONS ABOUT YOUR STUDENT ACCOUNT AND FINANCIAL AID

money.title: Overview of Student Accounts and Billing
money.what_it_is: The Office of the Bursar oversees all aspects of student accounts, including tuition billing, mandatory fees, payments, financial aid posting, and refunds.
money.who_to_contact: Office of the Bursar, Phone: '', Email: ''
money.timing: Billing begins in August for fall semester, January for spring semester, and May for summer semester.
money.notes: Students and authorized users receive an email notification when the student account balance is ready to view and pay.

money.title: Tuition Due Dates
money.what_it_is: This page provides information on tuition due dates and payment options for students at Penn State.
amounts: Installment due on August 31, 2026
Installment due on September 22, 2026
Installment due on October 22, 2026
Last installment due on November 22, 2026
money.timing: Fall semester: Early August; Spring semester: Early January; Summer Session: Early May
money.notes: Students will receive an email when their tuition balance is ready to view and pay in LionPATH. Families may choose to pay the full balance by the due date or enroll in a payment plan.

money.title: Fees and Charges
money.what_it_is: This page outlines various fees and charges applicable to students, including the Student Fee and International Undergraduate Student Fee.
steps: Log in to Student Home Base in LionPATH.
Click on 'My Finances' on top of the page.
Click on 'Permission to Use Federal Aid'.
Click on 'Grant Permission'.
Follow instructions to submit request.
amounts: $750 per semester for International Undergraduate Student Fee
75% of the full fee for part-time students registered for 5 but less than 9 credits
31% of the full fee for students registered for less than 5 credits
money.timing: Fees are charged immediately prior to the first day of the semester.
money.notes: Some fees cannot be paid with Federal Title IV financial aid funds.

money.title: Make a Payment
money.what_it_is: Instructions for making a payment on your student account.
steps: Log in to your Student Home Base in LionPATH
Click on 'My Finances' on top of the page
Select 'Manage My Account/Make A Payment' to get to your Student Account Dashboard
Click on 'Make a Payment' on the left side menu, and follow the instructions
money.notes: You can also use the 'Contact' option at the top of this page and use the 'Delinquent Tuition' category.

money.title: Payment Options
money.what_it_is: Penn State accepts various payment methods for tuition, including eCheck, credit card, international payments, and check or money order.
amounts: 2.25% service fee for credit card payments
$25 returned item fee for returned checks
$45 non-refundable administrative fee for Payment Plan
money.timing: Allow 5 business days for payment processing after receipt.
money.notes: Payments by credit card cannot be made via mail, phone, or in person. All international payments must be made through Flywire.

money.title: New Billing Portal Updates
money.what_it_is: Penn State launched a redesigned billing & payment portal in April 2026 to make managing student accounts easier and more intuitive.
steps: Log in to LionPATH to add Authorized Users and invite them to the new billing & payment portal.
Enroll in eRefund direct deposit.
Update and save any preferred payment methods after making your first payment.
Watch instructional videos to assist with completing these required steps.
money.who_to_contact: Bursar representative via the Contact Us option on the website; Flywire customer service: Domestic (US) +1(857) 287-3823, International (Canada): +1(857) 287-3818, Email: [email protected]
money.timing: The new student account billing and payment portal launched on April 28, 2026.
money.notes: Flywire supports both domestic and international payments.

money.title: Refund Policy
money.what_it_is: The refund policy outlines the conditions under which tuition payments and financial aid refunds are issued to students.
steps: Login to your Student Home Base in LionPATH
Click on 'My Finances' on top of the page
Select 'Manage My Account/Make A Payment' to get to the billing and payment portal
Navigate to the eRefunds tab
Enter and confirm your U.S. bank account information (routing and account number)
Agree to the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy and click 'Submit'
money.who_to_contact: For questions about a refund on your student account, please submit a contact us form.
amounts: Refunds by wire payment via Flywire is a refunding option available for international students residing outside of the United States
A refund will be issued to the parent if the amount of the Federal Direct Parent PLUS Loan exceeds the balance due of eligible charges on the student's account
money.timing: Penn State will refund the credit balance within TWO weeks of either the date the aid was credited to the student's account or the first day of the semester, whichever is later.
money.notes: Student account refunds are issued once per week.

money.title: Why have I not received my refund?
money.what_it_is: This page outlines possible reasons for not receiving a refund.
amounts: 14 days from receipt of that payment
money.timing: once weekly for paper refund checks
money.notes: eRefund is recommended for faster receipt of future refunds. Financial aid that has not yet disbursed is one possible cause — the Office of Student Aid (814-865-6301) handles disbursement.
money.source_title: Why have I not received my refund?

money.title: What is eRefund and how do I enroll in eRefund?
money.what_it_is: eRefund allows you to receive a refund due to you as a direct deposit into your U.S. checking or savings bank account. It is the fastest and most convenient way to receive your student refund.
steps: Login to your Student Home Base in LionPATH
Click on 'My Finances' on top of the page
Select 'Manage My Account/Make A Payment' to get to the billing and payment portal
Navigate to the eRefunds tab.
Enter and confirm your U.S. bank account information (routing and account number).
Agree to the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy and click 'Submit'.
money.timing: the process may take up to 3-5 business days before it will appear as a credit in your account
money.notes: Beginning summer 2026, Authorized Users will be able to enroll in eRefund to receive refunds from excess Direct Parent PLUS Loans funds only.
money.source_title: What is eRefund and how do I enroll in eRefund?

money.title: How do I get a refund of the credit balance on my account?
money.what_it_is: Student Account Refunds are issued once per week as determined by the Office of the Bursar.
steps: Enroll in eRefund for the quickest delivery of refunds.
money.timing: Refunds are issued once per week.
money.notes: If not enrolled in eRefund, the refund is issued as a paper check and sent by mail.
money.source_title: How do I get a refund of the credit balance on my account?

money.title: Delinquent Tuition
money.what_it_is: Delinquent tuition is an obligation that must be paid in a timely manner, and failure to do so may result in additional actions to collect the outstanding balance.
steps: Contact the office to discuss payment options.
Consider setting up a payment plan.
Make arrangements with Student Financial Services or a collection agency if necessary.
amounts: collection fees up to 40% of your balance
money.timing: Holds have been placed on your registration.
money.notes: Failure to make satisfactory arrangements may result in your account being placed with a licensed collection agency.

money.title: What happens if I do not pay my student account balance by the due date?
money.what_it_is: This page explains the consequences of not paying the student account balance by the due date, including late fees and holds.
amounts: 1.5% late fee
money.timing: up to 7-10 business days for mailed payments to be received and posted
money.notes: A financial hold will be placed on your Student Account if payment is not received by the due date.
money.source_title: What happens if I do not pay my student account balance by the due date?

money.title: Student Account Forms
money.what_it_is: This page provides various forms related to student accounts, including consent to release information and loan fund return requests.
money.notes: World Campus students should refer to the World Campus Employer Reimbursement and Tuition Deferment Program webpage.

money.title: Sponsored & Third-Party Billing
money.what_it_is: Sponsored billing & third-party billing is a financial sponsorship agreement by an organization, agency, or company foundation outside Penn State who makes a promise or commitment to pay for educational expenses on a student’s behalf.
steps: Submit a financial guarantee/voucher/letter of credit/billing authorization to the third-party billing team.
money.who_to_contact: Penn State Office of the Bursar, 103 Shields Building, 664 Curtin Road, University Park, PA 16802
amounts: Tuition
Mandatory Fees
Course fees (labs, music, art fees, etc.)
Health Insurance
Other fees
money.timing: Invoices are issued after the end of each semester’s add/drop deadline.
money.notes: Students are responsible for monitoring their official University email account for notifications regarding sponsored billing activity.

money.title: International Students
money.what_it_is: This page provides information for international students at Penn State regarding managing their student accounts and important processes to follow.
steps: Log in to LionPATH with your Penn State credentials.
Click on the 'My Finances' tab.
Select 'Manage My Account/Make A Payment' to open the billing and payment portal.
money.who_to_contact: Contact Us form on the website
amounts: a $45 non-refundable fee for enrolling in a Payment Plan
money.timing: Billing begins in early August for fall semester, January for spring semester, and May for summer semester.
money.notes: Important information will be communicated via Penn State email, and students should check their email regularly.

money.title: New Student Information
money.what_it_is: This page provides essential information for new students at Penn State regarding their student accounts and the steps to manage them.
steps: Log in to your MyPennState account to accept your offer of admission and pay your acceptance fees.
Log in to LionPATH with your Penn State credentials to access your Student Account.
Enroll in eRefund by navigating to the eRefunds tab in LionPATH and entering your U.S. bank account information.
Grant Authorized User access through LionPATH by adding their information in the Authorized Users section.
money.who_to_contact: Office of the Bursar, via the Contact Us form on the website.
amounts: 1.5% late fee
money.timing: Billing begins in early August for fall semester, January for spring semester, and May for summer semester.
money.notes: Important information will be communicated via Penn State email, and students should check their email regularly.

money.title: Can I pay by credit card?
money.what_it_is: Penn State accepts credit card payments online through LionPATH with a service fee.
amounts: 2.25% service fee
money.notes: Credit cards cannot be accepted by mail, phone, or in person.
money.source_title: Can I pay by credit card?
